title: Severe Cyclone Akvan: four seaports told to hoist signal 3
excerpt: Fishing boats in the northern Bay must shelter now. Heavy rain is possible in Khulna, Barishal and Chattogram divisions.
content:
Severe Cyclone Akvan is over the west-central Bay of Bengal and the adjoining south-west Bay, and the Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla and Payra seaports have been told to lower distant warning signal 2 and hoist local warning signal 3, the Bangladesh Meteorological Department said on Wednesday (18 November), bdnews24.com's Bangla edition reported.

At noon on Wednesday the storm was 1,235 km south-west of Chattogram port, 1,175 km from Cox's Bazar, 1,135 km from Mongla and 1,125 km from Payra. Sustained winds within 64 km of its centre reach 89 km/h, gusting to 117 km/h. It is moving north-north-west and may cross the North Andhra and South Odisha coast of India around noon on Friday.

All fishing boats and trawlers in the northern Bay have been told to go to safe shelter immediately and stay there until further notice. Moderate to heavy rain is possible in parts of Khulna, Barishal and Chattogram divisions.

Why it matters

Landfall is forecast in India, but rain and rough seas will reach the Bangladesh coast, including the Rohingya camps in Cox's Bazar. Fishing families lose income for every day boats stay ashore, and disaster response NGOs need to keep volunteers and stocks ready.

What to watch

The next Met Office bulletin, any change in the storm's track, rainfall in the coastal districts and the camps, and how long fishing stays suspended.
